Resolves #18652

Refs #18031

A tab reordered within a dock header now keeps naming its own item. `Neo.dashboard.dock.interaction.TabContainer#moveTo` moves the item id in the header's `dockItemIds` — on `sortZoneConfig` and on the live sort zone — before the generic move runs, and the `LayoutAdapter` `moveTo` listener reads the moved id from that live header instead of the node's projection-time `items`. A tab click, the next header drag, the reconciler pairing live cards with items and a second reorder all resolve the item the user sees.

Evidence: L2 (spec-driven: the unit tier and a real pointer on `examples/dashboard/dock` in Chromium, both red-first on unfixed dev) → L2 required (every AC runs in CI). No residuals.

## Deltas from ticket

- **The ticket body was corrected before this PR.** The first version credited the `swarm` activation to the Metrics click; the reorder had committed it, since a move activates the moved item, and the click changed nothing. The component arm therefore clicks a tab that is not live-active.
- **A second stale copy, with AC-2 for it.** The fix's first half left the second-reorder unit arm red: the listener's projection-time `items`, which a container reconciled in place keeps. The body names it; the listener now reads the live header.
- **The component arm runs the example with the bridge off.** A route sets `useAiClient: false`, so a local run registers no Neural Link session on a developer's bridge.
